description: Everything a monitor kept across its runs, newest first. Free. Filter by source. Returns { items, next_cursor }; next_cursor is null on the last page. To get only what is new since your last read, keep the first item_id you saw and stop paging when you reach it. Each item has item_id, run_id, source, url, title, text (cut to 1000 characters), author, published_at, score (0-100), signals (relevant and new_info, plus criteria, the lowest answer across the criteria, when the monitor has criteria; Meta ads have no new_info), found_at, and data by source: X likes, reposts, replies, views; Reddit subreddit, score, comments; YouTube channel, views, thumbnail; TikTok views, likes, comments, shares, saves, duration_s; Threads likes; Instagram likes, comments, views, media_type; Facebook reactions, comments, shares, views; Meta ads page, active, cta, link (the ad's landing page), platforms, thumbnail, with the ad headline as title and url the Ad Library record; web highlights, domain. TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook items also have post_id (the ID the API's GET /desearch/social/post gives the same post; an Instagram shortcode), type (video, image, carousel, reel, ...), hashtags, mentions (TikTok and Instagram), media (links to the post's videos and pictures), and thumbnail; media and thumbnail links expire after a few days. The metrics are the post's when the run found it. An item read from a watched account also has data.account, the name it was watched as, and one read from a watched hashtag has data.hashtag.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same source filter when you page.

monitor_id.description: monitor_id returned by monitor-create or monitor-list, example: '6f1d0c9e-0d55-4b8e-9a3c-3c4d9b8e2a10'.
